name: Incline Dumbbell Y-Raise
summary: A chest-supported shoulder raise performed on an incline bench with arms moving in a Y-formation to target the lower trapezius and lateral deltoids.

setup: Set an adjustable bench to an incline of 30 to 45 degrees.
Lie face down on the bench with your chest firmly supported and your head in a neutral position.
Hold a light dumbbell in each hand with your arms hanging down and thumbs pointed upward.
steps: Keeping your elbows nearly straight, raise the dumbbells diagonally upward and outward at roughly a 30- to 45-degree angle from your torso, forming a Y shape.
Lift until your arms align with your torso, feeling your lower and mid-trapezius contract.
Pause briefly at the top without shrugging your shoulders into your ears.
Lower the dumbbells smoothly under control back to the starting hanging position.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you raise the dumbbells into the Y position and inhale as you lower them.
cues: Form a Y, not a T.
Keep your shoulders down away from your ears.

common_faults.fault: Excessively shrugging the shoulders upward using the upper traps.
common_faults.correction: Depress your shoulder blades before raising and focus on rotating the scapulae upward rather than shrugging.

common_faults.fault: Using momentum or arching the lower back off the bench.
common_faults.correction: Keep your chest glued to the pad and select lighter dumbbells to isolate the movement.

common_faults.fault: Raising the arms straight out to the sides into a T shape instead of a Y.
common_faults.correction: Angle your arms roughly 30 to 45 degrees forward into the scapular plane.

precautions: Use very light weights to protect the rotator cuff and avoid neck strain.
